prompt:
YOU ARE HEADLESS. There is no next turn: nothing will wake you, and any background job you
start dies when you exit. Run every slow step SYNCHRONOUSLY, in the foreground, and do not
finish until the work actually exists on disk. Never background a render and yield. Never wait
on a notification. Slower is fine; ending your turn with the job unfinished is not.

One more rehearsal before opening night: a tiny book called The Encore. One spread plus cover and closing plate, locked characters only, at most 3 image generations, the universe's own chain with every gate, stop after the local render passes. No publishing.

You have superpowers.

</SUBAGENT-STOP>

<EXTREMELY-IMPORTANT>
If you think there is even a 1% chance a skill might apply to what you are doing, you ABSOLUTELY MUST invoke the skill.

IF A SKILL APPLIES TO YOUR TASK, YOU DO NOT HAVE A CHOICE. YOU MUST USE IT.

This is not negotiable. You cannot rationalize your way out of this.
</EXTREMELY-IMPORTANT>

## The Rule

**Invoke relevant or requested skills BEFORE any response or action** — including clarifying questions, exploring the codebase, or checking files. If it turns out wrong for the situation, you don't have to use it.

**Before entering plan mode:** if you haven't already brainstormed, invoke the brainstorming skill first.

Then announce "Using [skill] to [purpose]" and follow the skill exactly. If it has a checklist, create a todo per item.

## Skill Priority

When multiple skills apply, process skills come first — they set the approach, then implementation skills (frontend-design, etc.) carry it out. Brainstorming and systematic-debugging are Superpowers' most common process skills, but the rule holds for any of them.

- "Let's build X" → superpowers:brainstorming first, then implementation skills.
- "Fix this bug" → superpowers:systematic-debugging first, then domain skills.

## Red Flags

These thoughts mean STOP—you're rationalizing:

| Thought | Reality |
|---------|---------|
| "This is just a simple question" | Questions are tasks. Check for skills. |
| "I need more context first" | Skill check comes BEFORE clarifying questions. |
| "Let me explore the codebase first" | Skills tell you HOW to explore. Check first. |
| "I can check git/files quickly" | Files lack conversation context. Check for skills. |
| "Let me gather information first" | Skills tell you HOW to gather information. |
| "This doesn't need a formal skill" | If a skill exists, use it. |
| "I remember this skill" | Skills evolve. Read current version. |
| "This doesn't count as a task" | Action = task. Check for skills. |
| "The skill is overkill" | Simple things become complex. Use it. |
| "I'll just do this one thing first" | Check BEFORE doing anything. |
| "This feels productive" | Undisciplined action wastes time. Skills prevent this. |
| "I know what that means" | Knowing the concept ≠ using the skill. Invoke it. |

## Platform Adaptation

If your harness appears here, read its reference file for special instructions:

- Codex: `references/codex-tools.md`
- Pi: `references/pi-tools.md`
- Antigravity: `references/antigravity-tools.md`

## User Instructions

User instructions (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, GEMINI.md, etc, direct requests) take precedence over skills, which in turn override default behavior. Only skip skill workflows or instructions when your human partner has explicitly told you to.
</EXTREMELY_IMPORTANT>"
  }
}

content.text: Using the make-a-hyperagent-book skill to run The Encore through the universe's own chain. First, reading the global AGENTS.md as required.

input.command: cat ~/.agents/AGENTS.md
input.description: Read global agent instructions

input.args: The Encore — a tiny rehearsal book: one spread plus cover and closing plate, locked characters only, at most 3 image generations, full chain with every gate, stop after local render passes, no publishing

commands.name: add-appliedai-wiki-qa
commands.description: Add a Question & Answer article to the Questions & Answers section of appliedai.wiki (docs/questions/, slug /questions). Takes a real question someone asked (screenshot, paste, transcript, or braindump) plus optional source material, and produces a Q&A page where the H1 IS the question and the body is a detailed, cross-linked answer in the wiki's voice. Anonymizes questioners by default, fact-checks any claim about AI products against current behavior, generates a hero comic, builds, commits, and pushes. Use when Gary says "add a Q&A to appliedai", "answer this question on the wiki", "field question for appliedai.wiki", or pastes a real question he wants answered there. This is the Q&A-specialized variant of intake-field-note-into-garys-wikis. (user)

commands.name: add-biographical-screenshot
commands.description: Add one or more screenshots to Gary's biographical-screenshots collection at garys-freedom/docs/misc-collections/biographical-screenshots/ — a chronological screenshot photo book of life moments as they appeared on his screens. Auto-reads when each screenshot was taken from file metadata, copies it in with a dated name, writes an annotation in Gary's voice from his braindump plus what is visible in the image, cross-links PRM files for people who appear, inserts the entry in chronological position, commits, and pushes. Use when Gary says "add this to biographical screenshots", "biographical screenshot this", "add this screenshot to the photo book", "/add-biographical-screenshot <path>", or hands over a screenshot of a call/chat/moment with a story attached. NOT for press photos (press-gallery), NOT for testimonies (capture-testimonial), and NOT for processing the conversation itself into PRM (garysheng-process-transcript). (user)

commands.name: add-inspiration-book
commands.description: Add a book, transcript, essay, script, or series to Gary's "Inspiration" reading shelf at garys-freedom/docs/misc-collections/inspiration-library/. Accepts EITHER an already-text source (ebook .txt/.md, .pdf) OR a raw audio/video file (e.g. a Libation-liberated audiobook .m4b) which it transcribes locally first with anti-loop settings on by default. Names the file by the shelf convention, copies it in, and updates the README index (chronological row + theme section). Use when Gary says "add this book to inspiration", "add to my reading shelf", "transcribe this audiobook onto the shelf", "/add-inspiration-book <file>", or hands over any book source to file onto the shelf. NOT for the garysheng.com /inspo page (use garysheng-add-inspo) or the private shadow inspo (use garysheng-add-shadow-inspo). (user)

commands.name: add-jarvis-integration-to-curated-repo
commands.description: Add a new integration recipe to Gary's curated-jarvis-integrations bank, or update an existing one. Researches the current best CLI/MCP options for the service, scaffolds folder-per-skill shape (INTEGRATE.md + SKILL.md + scripts/ + package.json), bumps the README status table, commits, and pushes. Use when Gary says "add a notion integration", "update the create-or-update-google-doc recipe", "add jarvis integration for X", or invokes /add-jarvis-integration-to-curated-repo. (user)

commands.name: add-source-to-source-bootstrapped-wiki
commands.description: Intake a new foundational source (book, manuscript, long-form transcript, video series, or URL set) into an EXISTING source-bootstrapped wiki: a Docusaurus wiki with a foundations/concepts/perspectives/sources IA and a repo-root SOURCES.md, like exitstrategy.wiki. Normalizes the source into gitignored sources-raw/, extracts a structural source map into .ingest/, writes the faithful sources/<slug>.md map page, MERGES the source into the existing concept canon (enriching existing concept pages with the new author's voice and adding genuinely new concept pages), adds new perspectives or sharpens existing tensions, harvests new glossary terms, adds the bibliography row to SOURCES.md, wires the sidebar, and runs the build. Use when Gary says "intake this book into <wiki>", "add this source to the wiki", "add <book> to exitstrategy-wiki", "fold this transcript into the wiki", or hands over a book/transcript file alongside a source-bootstrapped wiki repo path. NOT for scaffolding a brand-new wiki (use start-new-wiki), NOT for a single field-note article on the SupersuitUp wikis (use intake-field-note-into-garys-wikis), and NOT for personal reading-shelf filing (use add-inspiration-book). (user)

commands.name: add-to-spare-cycles
commands.description: Use when Gary names a valuable but non-urgent task to do later when he has excess token budget to spend. Triggers include "add this to the shelf", "put that on spare cycles", "nice-to-have for later", "one for when I have spare tokens", or any time a worthwhile improvement surfaces that should not interrupt the current work. Also the place to look when Gary says he has budget to burn. (user)

commands.name: agent-browser
commands.description: Automates browser interactions for web testing, form filling, screenshots, and data extraction. Use when the user needs to navigate websites, interact with web pages, fill forms, take screenshots, test web applications, or extract information from web pages. (user)

commands.name: ai-sdk
commands.description: Answer questions about the AI SDK and help build AI-powered features. Use when developers: (1) Ask about AI SDK functions like generateText, streamText, ToolLoopAgent, embed, or tools, (2) Want to build AI agents, chatbots, RAG systems, or text generation features, (3) Have questions about AI providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, etc.), streaming, tool calling, structured output, or embeddings, (4) Use React hooks like useChat or useCompletion. Triggers on: "AI SDK", "Vercel AI SDK", "generateText", "streamText", "add AI to my app", "build an agent", "tool calling", "structured output", "useChat". (user)

commands.name: apify-js-sdk
commands.description: Apify JS SDK Documentation - Web scraping, crawling, and Actor development (user)

commands.name: apify-ultimate-scraper
commands.description: Universal AI-powered web scraper for any platform. Scrape data from Instagram, Facebook, TikTok, YouTube, Google Maps, Google Search, Google Trends, Booking.com, and TripAdvisor. Use for lead generation, brand monitoring, competitor analysis, influencer discovery, trend research, content analytics, audience analysis, or any data extraction task. (user)

commands.name: apple-contacts-lookup
commands.description: Query macOS Contacts database to match phone numbers to contact names. Use when you need to identify who a phone number belongs to from iMessage, call logs, or any other source. (user)

commands.name: applied-ai-field-notes
commands.description: Use when Gary shares a YouTube video, article URL, podcast, PDF, or audio from a "note-sharer" firm (consultancy, lab, VC, or any org that publicly shares applied-AI fieldwork like BOI, BCG, McKinsey, a16z, Sequoia, OpenAI, Anthropic) and wants to process their advice into structured field-note artifacts on appliedai.wiki. Also triggers on "/applied-ai-field-notes <url>", "field note this", "add to note-sharers", "process this <firm> video", or any URL from a known applied-AI thought-leader org. (user)

commands.name: approve-and-continue
commands.description: Gary's "green light, keep going" signal. Use whenever Gary approves work in progress — "good job", "nice", "looks great", "I like it", "love it", "go forward", "ship it", "perfect", "lgtm", a thumbs up — WITH OR WITHOUT inline edits attached. Behavior: apply any edits he included FIRST, then autonomously do the next logical step of the workflow without stopping to ask permission. It is the opposite of a hard stop: approval of one unit is approval to carry the momentum to the next unit, not to idle for confirmation. (user)

commands.name: archive-desktop
commands.description: Sweep all loose clutter off Gary's macOS Desktop into a dated "YYYY-MM-DD Desktop Archive" folder tucked inside the current month-year holder folder (e.g. "July 2026"). Never deletes anything — the Desktop is treated as a rolling time capsule, so files are moved and preserved, never destroyed. Leaves month-year holder folders and system dotfiles alone. Use when Gary says "clean my desktop", "archive my desktop", "tidy the desktop", "sweep the desktop", "/archive-desktop", or when the Desktop has accumulated loose screenshots, downloads, exports, and stray folders. (user)

commands.name: audit-model-deprecations
commands.description: Find deprecated LLM model ids across Gary's repos, verify every replacement against the live provider API before proposing it, and migrate on his go-ahead. Reports renames separately from version jumps, because only one of those is safe to apply mechanically. Use when Gary asks "is my Gemini model current", "any deprecated models", "check model deprecations", "/audit-model-deprecations", when a provider announces a shutdown, or on the weekly coherence run. NOT for choosing a model on quality or price. (user)

commands.name: auto-transcribe
commands.description: Transcribe voice memos with automatic speaker identification using Deepgram Nova-3 + pyannoteAI voiceprints (user)

commands.name: bible-character-assessment
commands.description: Scan a user's local markdown files (context lake / Jarvis workspace) and determine which Bible character they most resemble. A zero-question personality assessment. Use when someone says "which Bible character am I", "run the Bible assessment", "Bible character quiz", or wants to see what their context lake reveals about them. (user)

commands.name: calling-calculator
commands.description: Discern a believer's divine calling using the FaithWalk OS Calling Calculator framework. Conducts a structured interview across the Conference of Influences (burden, prompting, community confirmation, providence, Scripture, prophetic words, sanctified desire), filters candidates against Scripture and kingdom fruit, surfaces 1-3 Calling Candidates with convergence scores and next obedient steps, and auto-writes a strategic-document artifact to garys-freedom. Use when Gary says "calling calculator", "discern my calling", "run the calling calculator on X", "what is X's calling", or when someone sits down to discern their divine assignment. Never claims to hear God for the user. The Holy Spirit has final say. (user)

commands.name: capture-testimonial
commands.description: Capture a testimony from someone whose life was positively impacted by Gary's work (a picture book, an AI training or workshop, a wiki, coaching) into garys-freedom/docs/misc-collections/testimonies/. Preserves the raw audio or video FIRST, transcribes locally, writes the testimony verbatim in the speaker's own voice, cross-links their PRM file, and drafts a thank-you plus a permission ask. Use when Gary says "capture this testimonial", "log this testimony", "someone sent me a voice memo about the book", "add this to testimonies", "/capture-testimonial", or forwards praise from a real person about something he made. NOT for prophetic words spoken over Gary (that is garysheng-prophetic-word) and NOT for general PRM interaction logging (that is garysheng-process-transcript). (user)

commands.name: cdp-screenshot
commands.description: Screenshot any URL with real device emulation (mobile included) using a throwaway headless Chrome driven over the DevTools protocol with Node's built-in WebSocket. No puppeteer, no playwright, no MCP. Use when the chrome-devtools MCP profile is locked by another session, when you need TRUE mobile-viewport rendering (bare --window-size headless enforces a ~600px minimum layout width and silently crops, which fakes overflow bugs), or when you need full-page capture plus a machine-readable horizontal-overflow report. Trigger phrases: "screenshot this url", "mobile screenshot", "is this page overflowing", "devtools mcp is locked". (user)

commands.name: chatgpt-deep-research
commands.description: Run a multi-source agentic deep-research task using OpenAI's `o3-deep-research` or `o4-mini-deep-research` model via the Responses API. The model browses the web, fetches documents, optionally runs code or hits remote MCP servers, and returns a structured report with inline citations. Use when Gary says "/chatgpt-deep-research <question>", "deep research X", "run a deep research on Y", "have ChatGPT research Z for me", or wants OpenAI-grade multi-minute research that goes well beyond a single WebSearch call. NOT for quick lookups (use WebSearch / WebFetch) and NOT for transcribing or summarizing a known source (use garysheng-content-summary). (user)

commands.name: chatgpt-images
commands.description: Generate or edit images using OpenAI's gpt-image-2 model. Use when you need high-quality image generation or editing with OpenAI's API. Supports text-to-image generation and image editing with a reference photo. (user)

commands.name: cofacilitate-supersuit-1on1
commands.description: Live co-pilot for running a 1:1 Supersuit Up session in real time. You drive Gary through the session segment by segment: announce where you are, hand him the exact next move (the provoke, the Socratic ladder, the practice beat), then wait while he voice-dictates (Wispr Flow) what actually happened, react to it, capture live notes, keep time, and advance to the next step when the segment's goal is hit. Loads the prep dossier as the run-of-show. Invoked as /cofacilitate-supersuit-1on1 <person>. Use when Gary says "be my co-pilot for a session", "co-pilot this session", "run the 1:1 with me", "facilitate this live", "start the session", or is mid-session feeding in what just happened. (user)

commands.name: combine-iphone-videos
commands.description: Concatenate all iPhone videos on the Desktop (or any folder) into one combined video file, in chronological order by filename. Handles the messy reality of iPhone clips — mixed codecs (HEVC/H.264), mixed frame rates (24/30/60/120fps), mixed AND MIS-TAGGED orientation, and clips carrying junk metadata streams — by auditing orientation visually, normalizing every clip to one common format, then doing a lossless stream-copy join. Use when Gary says "combine my iPhone videos", "concat the movs on my desktop", "stitch these clips into one video", "/combine-iphone-videos", or after AirDropping a batch of phone videos to the Desktop. One activation replaces the old two-step rename-then-concat flow. (user)

commands.name: comic-strip
commands.description: Generate a Marvel-zine action-comic strip on any topic via gpt-image-2. Variable panel count (matches the content's beats; don't force 4). Cream paper background, bold inked outlines, crimson + cobalt + gold accents. Optional high-tech power-armor DNA (arc-reactor cyan, helmet-visor POV, gauntlet) for Supersuit / hyperagency / AI-augmentation topics. ALWAYS pass the canonical reference images as --input-image flags to lock the visual style (two style refs) and the character identity of the supersuited leader (one character sheet). Use when summarizing an article, doc, transcript, advice, framework, or concept as a comic — for wikis, blogs, slides, social, posters, or PRM artifacts. (user)

commands.name: compounding-intake
commands.description: Intake new thinking into compounding.wiki, an authored-canon wiki (The operational toolshelf: the specific tools, setups, and hacks that compound a more fruitful, enjoyable digital life.). Authored-canon mode means you author net-new original philosophy that must cohere with the existing canon, in the wiki's own voice. Use when someone says "add this to compounding.wiki", "concept for compounding.wiki", "compounding-intake", or "/compounding-intake", or hands over a braindump, transcript, or idea for this wiki. NOT for faithfully mapping external sources (that is source-grounded mode). (user)

commands.name: crank-blessing-book
commands.description: Claim and produce one blessing-day picture book, tracking state so a fleet of separate chats can chew through the 17-book backlog in parallel without stepping on each other. Auto-claims the next open book and starts building immediately — never asks Gary which book to take, and never treats books already claimed by other chats as a blocker. Reads the run manifest, atomically claims the next unbuilt book (or a named one), pulls its brief from the blessing-day book backlog doc, and drives it through make-a-nof-book honoring the batch's frame (Apostle Delmar as himself, Jerry the default learner, Miriam's household for the story books), updating a per-book status file at every phase and pausing only at make-a-nof-book's three real gates. Use when Gary says "crank the next blessing book", "claim a book", "/crank-blessing-book", "make the next book from the backlog", or wants the board of what's built. NOT for a book outside this batch (use make-a-nof-book directly) and NOT for editing the backlog doc. (user)

commands.name: create-brand-os-picture-book
commands.description: Build a brand-OS-powered, all-ages illustrated flip-book (manuscript -> brand OS -> spread-by-spread illustration -> listen-along narration -> reader). Use when Gary wants to make an illustrated gift/primer book like The Golden Path or An Honest Primer on AI. Leans on generate-a-brand-os for the visual canon and chatgpt-images for illustration. Narration (one-narrator listen-along, ElevenLabs) is a default, not an add-on. DELIVERY DEFAULTS TO THE SHARED PLATFORM (picture-book-platform) — a manifest + assets + one registry line against the shared reader; forking a per-book Next.js site is a supported option, not the default. (user)

commands.name: create-calendar-event
commands.description: Create a Google Calendar event on Gary's calendar via the gog CLI, optionally inviting attendees. Use when Gary says "add this to my calendar", "put it on my calendar", "schedule X", "calendar invite", or shares an event flyer/screenshot to be turned into a calendar entry. Handles attendee email lookup from PRM, image (HEIC/PNG/JPG) parsing, timezone normalization, and post-create updates. (user)

commands.name: create-context-page
commands.description: Generate a context-complete page at garysheng.com/note/<slug> that Gary sends a friend so his accompanying text can be one link. The page bakes in ALL the context: it can explain something, make an offer, or wrap other links (typically both prose plus link cards). Given a purpose and a person, it composes an ordered list of typed blocks (prose, link cards, callout, steps, paste-in prompt, image), optionally generates on-brand images, appends a ContextPage entry to the mypersonalwebsite repo, builds, commits, and pushes (auto-deploys). Use when Gary says "make a page for X", "create a /note page", "context page for X", "a page I can send that explains Y", "wrap these links in a page", or "/create-context-page". NOT just for bio offers (that is one seed example); this is the general "send-a-friend-a-page-with-full-context" pattern. (user)

commands.name: create-email-video-thumbnail
commands.description: Turn a video into an email-ready clickable thumbnail: a short looping GIF with a play button and runtime badge, plus a static fallback and the hyperlink instructions. Use when Gary says "embed this video in an email", "make a GIF thumbnail for this video", "clickable GIF that links to the Descript/Loom/YouTube video", "video preview for a newsletter", or "/create-email-video-thumbnail <file>". Handles the Gmail-inline path and the HTML-email path. (user)

commands.name: create-global-skill
commands.description: Registers a skill so Claude Code and OpenClaw can discover it, via symlinks to ~/.claude/skills/ and ~/.openclaw/workspace/skills/. Bias toward the skill living hyperlocally in the repo it concerns ({repo}/skills/{name}/) with a global pointer at ~/.agents/skills/; only truly cross-repo skills live directly in ~/.agents/skills/. Accepts a skill name or a full path to an existing repo-local skill folder. (user)

commands.name: create-microautobiography
commands.description: Generate an AI-narrated microautobiography site for a person — chapters of their life story read aloud by an ElevenLabs narrator with music, live waveform, and click-any-sentence playback — by running a structured life interview and filling the SupersuitUp/microautobiography-template. Use when someone says "make me a bio site like Gary's", "create my microautobiography", "/create-microautobiography", "I want an AI-narrated life story page", or Gary is Supersuiting someone up and their story deserves a narrated home. Worked example: garysheng.com/bio. (user)

commands.name: create-misc-collection
commands.description: Stand up a NEW miscellaneous collection in garys-freedom/docs/misc-collections/ — the folder, a README that defines the collection's conventions (entry format, naming, ordering, cross-link rules), an optional images/ or raw/ subfolder, AND the companion repo-local add-* skill that files future entries, registered globally via symlinks. Optionally seeds the first entries from whatever Gary hands over. Use when Gary says "create a new misc collection", "new collection for X", "I want to start collecting Y", "/create-misc-collection", or describes a new recurring category of life artifacts (screenshots, quotes, receipts, moments) that doesn't fit an existing collection. NOT for adding an entry to an existing collection (use that collection's own add-* skill) and NOT for strategic documents (garysheng-create-doc). (user)

commands.name: create-or-update-google-doc
commands.description: Create or update Google Docs from markdown/HTML content with image support. Uses gog CLI for OAuth. (user)

commands.name: create-storybrand-site
commands.description: Scaffold a polished marketing website for a person or small business using the latest Next.js + Tailwind v4, with the page built on Donald Miller's StoryBrand SB7 framework and the copy written in stupid-simple marketing voice. Use when Gary says "create a StoryBrand site for X", "build a landing page for X", "make a website for my friend X", "spin up a marketing site for X", or describes a person/offer that needs a clarity-first one-page site. Casts the customer as the hero and the business as the guide; every section maps to an SB7 beat; all copy lives in one typed content file so it is trivial to edit. NOT for wikis (use start-new-wiki), NOT for refining copy in isolation (use storybrand-refine). (user)

commands.name: create-strategic-document-base
commands.description: Base protocol for creating any strategic document (thesis, memo, proposal, artifact, wiki post, public doc). Enforces interrogative interview, project routing, context gathering, style guardrails, and post-draft validation. Referenced by all project-specific strategic doc skills (garysheng-create-doc, divine-principle-spec, faithwalk-os). Invoke directly only if no project-specific skill fits; normally delegated to by a project skill. (user)

commands.name: abu:abu
commands.description: (abu) THE FRONT DOOR to Agentic Brand Universe. Hand it nothing and it reports where your brand universe stands, what the single highest-leverage next move is, and a ten-minute one if you are bored. Hand it a wish in plain language ("make a zine cover", "my characters look different every time", "I want this to feel more like my brand") and it routes to the right verb without you knowing any verbs exist. Use when someone says "abu", "how's my universe", "where am I", "what should I do next", "what can I do", "I'm bored", "get me to 100", "status", or opens a session cold with no idea what to ask for. Also the correct destination whenever you catch yourself about to show a non-technical user a shell command. Universe-agnostic; resolves the target universe itself.

commands.name: abu:add-character
commands.description: (abu) Add ONE character to an Agentic Brand Universe: interview the source (a real person's story/wardrobe/sensitive-list, or a fictional design brief), reuse-first via casting sweep, then scaffold a typed `character` entity with the SPEC §12 reference-matrix slots (8 shots) and a ready-to-run generation prompt per shot. Real people get a photo stack and a subject-approval gate; art is NOT generated here (that is `shoot-references`). Use when adding a person/character to a universe. Generic and universe-parameterized: pass the target universe.

commands.name: abu:add-generator
commands.description: (abu) Add ONE deterministic generator to a universe (SPEC v0.13 §4.11) — code that DRAWS an asset instead of prompting for one. Use for anything whose correctness is a NUMBER rather than a judgement: a mark, a favicon set, a starfield, procedural clouds, grids, scale rules, colour-chip sheets, diagram furniture, share-card frames. Scaffolds generators/<id>/ with a typed generator.json (params, seed, inputs, outputs, install map, proof), an entrypoint that writes provenance recipes, and a proof sheet rendered at REAL size for a human to approve. Also the correct fix when you catch yourself writing a loose make_*.py beside an asset, hand-copying a generated file into several sites, or prompting an image model for something you could compute. Generic and universe-parameterized: pass the target universe.

commands.name: abu:add-motif
commands.description: (abu) Add ONE motif (a recurring visual element, gesture, or pattern that must render identically wherever it appears, not a one-off image) to an Agentic Brand Universe (interview what it is and its load-bearing detail, reuse-first via casting sweep, then scaffold a typed `motif` entity with SPEC §12's hero + detail reference slots and ready-to-run generation prompts). Art is NOT generated here (that is `shoot-references`). Use when a repeating visual pattern needs to stay consistent across many renders. Generic and universe-parameterized: pass the target universe.

commands.name: abu:add-prop
commands.description: (abu) Add ONE prop (a discrete physical object a character holds, wears, or uses, that must render identically wherever it appears) to an Agentic Brand Universe (interview what it is and its load-bearing detail, reuse-first via casting sweep, then scaffold a typed `prop` entity with SPEC §12's hero + detail reference slots and ready-to-run generation prompts). Art is NOT generated here (that is `shoot-references`). Use when a specific object needs to stay consistent across many renders. Generic and universe-parameterized: pass the target universe.

commands.name: abu:add-relation
commands.description: (abu) Record ONE typed relation between two ids in an Agentic Brand Universe's canon graph (`crossover-with`, `appears-in`, `derived-from`, `contradicts`, `supersedes`) as a `from`/`rel`/`to`/`story`/`note` record written to `canon/relations/`. Keeps the graph queryable (every crossover, every story touching a doctrine) and makes contradictions and supersessions explicit records instead of silent edits to history. Art is NOT touched by this skill at all. Use whenever two canon entities, or an entity and a story, need a recorded relationship. Generic and universe-parameterized: pass the target universe.

commands.name: abu:add-setting
commands.description: (abu) Add ONE setting (a location) to an Agentic Brand Universe (interview its fixed geometry, fixed camera angles, and dressing, reuse-first via casting sweep, then scaffold a typed `setting` entity with SPEC §12's contract slots (turnaround, per-angle empty plates, blueprint, plus map/blocking/dressing descriptor prose) and ready-to-run generation prompts). Stays `status: unlocked` (correctly refused by the render gate) until `shoot-references` fills the plates and you lock it. Art is NOT generated here. Use when a story needs to render into a location. Generic and universe-parameterized: pass the target universe.

commands.name: abu:add-story
commands.description: (abu) Add ONE story to an Agentic Brand Universe as a typed StorySpec (a medium-neutral work over canon, NOT an `add-entity` kind). Interview the logline, its declared spine (obedient-servant, thesis, primer, testimony, or another open-set value; a story is never assumed to be a hero-journey), its refrain, its register (defaults to the universe's `identity.register`, with a per-story override allowed), and its beats with per-beat provenance. Registers as `status: "stub"` (logline + spine only) or `"full"` (features + beats + provenance filled). Runs a casting sweep over the beats' named entities and hands off anything not yet in canon to add-character/add-setting/add-visual-metaphor/add-motif/add-prop. Art is NOT generated here. Use when composing a new property (book, chapter, or other unit) out of existing or new canon. Generic and universe-parameterized: pass the target universe.

commands.name: abu:add-visual-metaphor
commands.description: (abu) Add ONE visual metaphor (a spine-object a whole property argues through, not merely a location) to an Agentic Brand Universe (interview the object and the states it argues across, reuse-first via casting sweep, then scaffold a typed `visual-metaphor` entity with SPEC §12's setting-style contract: a locked master plus per-state plates, and map/blocking/dressing descriptor prose). Stays `status: unlocked` (correctly refused by the render gate) until `shoot-references` fills the plates and you lock it. Art is NOT generated here. Use when a story is built by zooming into one recurring object across changing states. Generic and universe-parameterized: pass the target universe.

commands.name: abu:book-doctor
commands.description: (abu) Grade a RENDERED book on local disk against what its render-spec declares, BEFORE it is delivered anywhere. Checks that every declared spread exists, that the endcaps (front cover and closing plate) are portrait while interiors are landscape, that every generated asset carries its provenance recipe, that no spread was generated from another spread render, and optionally that every cast entity is registered and locked. Deliberately knows nothing about any delivery surface: no bucket, no CDN, no reader URL, no network, no API key. Use when Gary says "book doctor", "is this book done", "check the book", "grade this book", "/book-doctor", or before declaring ANY rendered book finished. Complements assert-story (pre-render gate, no output yet to measure), lint-universe (static warnings) and universe-doctor (grades the whole universe); a delivery platform's own doctor probing its storage is a separate, platform-owned tool and the two do not overlap.

commands.name: abu:canon-resolve
commands.description: (abu) Before writing ANY render prompt in an Agentic Brand Universe, resolve every named character, setting, and motif to its canon entity: output the locked sheet paths (requiredForRender), the invariants to enforce, and the entity's prose rules, then run the load-bearing gate (assert.sh spread|story). Prevents reinventing locked designs, passing draft or wrong-era references, and prompting from memory. Generic and universe-parameterized: pass the target universe.

commands.name: abu:casting-sweep
commands.description: (abu) Before naming any NEW character, setting, or motif in a story, sweep the universe's canon for an existing entity that fits the role natively, and emit a casting table (each role: reuse an entity id, or NEW plus a one-line justification). Reuse wins by default: it saves the whole reference-matrix build and every reuse is a crossover receipt. Generic and universe-parameterized: pass the target universe.

commands.name: abu:compose-spec
commands.description: (abu) Scaffold and RE-SYNC a book's render-spec from its StorySpec, filling everything canon determines, enumerating every legal choice canon constrains, and never overwriting authored scene text. Use when starting a new book's render-spec, after adding or removing a beat, after shooting a new plate or wardrobe look, or whenever you catch yourself hand-writing a per-book authoring script. Trigger phrases: "scaffold the render-spec", "re-sync the spec", "compose-spec", "the spec is out of date with the story", "I added a beat".

commands.name: abu:compose-spread
commands.description: (abu) Render ONE spread of an Agentic Brand Universe book as an atomic unit — resolve canon, deterministically ASSEMBLE the prompt + refs from canon (register-anchor-first, each in-frame entity's block for its SELECTED look including alt-looks, auto-disambiguation, and negatives COMPUTED from the selected looks so a blanket negative can never fight a canon alt-look), generate, then read back. This is the atomic step render-book and update-book used to describe in prose and every book re-hand-rolled as its own gen-spread.py. Character/setting truth is read from canon/entities, never retyped per book. Generic and universe-parameterized.

commands.name: abu:cover
commands.description: (abu) Create a picture-book cover for a story in an Agentic Brand Universe, at the platform's portrait aspect. Bakes the diegetic title + the universe mark (identity.mark), passes the register anchor first, and runs render-readback on the title spelling + hero likeness + register discipline. Generic and universe-parameterized.

commands.name: abu:create-form
commands.description: (abu) Author a NEW form (a new KIND of work) for an Agentic Brand Universe, extracted from works ACTUALLY MADE, never speculated. Scaffolds forms/<id>/ (FORM.md + PROMPT.md + optional evals/) via a scaffolder that REFUSES on zero evidence, then guides the distillation (FORM.md states the evidence base, PROMPT.md is the method with gates and scripts named at the step that uses them, evals verified against the goldens they claim to reproduce) and the backfill (each evidence work gains a work.json declaration with a retrofit note; no historical record is ever rewritten). Built on three precedents: fashion-look (a newborn form), living-diorama (a growing one), and the book chain (compose-spec, compose-spread, judge-slot, book-doctor, update-book), which is the CHIEF precedent: a form at full maturity, and the trajectory every form grows along. Use when someone says "create a form", "author a new form", "extract a form from these works", "this kind of work keeps recurring", or when make-a-work has no form for a kind of work that already exists as finished pieces. NOT for making a work in an existing form (abu:make-a-work) and NOT for rendering a book (abu:make-a-book owns that chain today).

commands.name: abu:create-lookbook
commands.description: (abu) Scaffold a Lookbook (SPEC §4.7.1) — a portable folder (lookbook.json + refs/) that defines a curated but intentionally VARIED visual vocabulary (a wardrobe/fashion, a range of building silhouettes, a set of faces), the complement of a Style Pack. Use when a recurring aspect must stay on-aesthetic yet DIFFER per instance, and modeling it as a motif/prop (which force sameness) or a Style Pack (a render medium) is wrong. It writes 4-12 varied exemplars, a varietyRule (the "vary, never clone" instruction), and a read-back gate that checks for variety. Consumed by on-brand-image via --lookbook, and bound to a universe through a craft-canon register-rule that names it. Invoke via create-lookbook, "make a lookbook", "build a fashion/wardrobe aesthetic", or when you catch yourself wanting variety from a primitive that enforces sameness.

commands.name: abu:create-style-pack
commands.description: (abu) Scaffold a Style Pack (SPEC §4.7) — a portable folder (pack.json + refs/) that defines ONE look and is consumable by on-brand-image with no universe. Use when you have a set of blessed images that share a look and want to make more that match (a register's paint-language extracted into a reusable artifact), or when a universe's register should source its anchor + rejected poles from a shared pack. Copies the refs INTO the pack (self-contained), writes the manifest with a load-bearing read-back gate, and validates. Pairs with on-brand-image (which consumes the pack) and shoot-references (locked masters passed alongside). Invoke via create-style-pack, "make a style pack", "extract this look into a pack", or as the fix when you catch yourself generating on-brand images with no pack (a look with no Style Pack is the gap evolve-agentic-story names).

commands.name: abu:evolve-abu
commands.description: (abu) Evolve the Agentic Brand Universe framework itself — its skills, engine, spec, templates, and plugin — instead of hand-rolling around its gaps. Invoke mid-session the moment you catch yourself (or Gary catches you) doing framework-shaped work by hand: a bespoke generate/provenance script, a manual step you keep repeating, a missing scaffolder (e.g. no create-style-pack), a look with no Style Pack, provenance saved by memory instead of by tool. The framework is young and WILL be missing things; hand-rolling once is fine, hand-rolling twice is a bug in the framework. This skill promotes the hand-rolled thing UP into the framework, bumps the version, ships it, logs it, and updates itself. Use when Gary says "why are we hand-rolling this", "update the framework/templates/skills", "fix the generator", "we know better", "/evolve-abu", or is visibly frustrated that a repeated manual action should be a tool.

commands.name: abu:judge-slot
commands.description: (abu) Judge one generated slot against an entity's locked golden, item by item over its declared invariants, in a context that has NOT been told how the slot was made. A ROLE, not a service: fill it with a subagent, a fresh session, a human, or simply another turn inside the composer. Returns PASS or DEFECT per invariant with evidence, and fails closed. Use after generating any slot bound to a canon entity that declares invariants.

commands.name: abu:land-work
commands.description: (abu) Merge a finished work branch home instead of leaving it parked, in ANY git repo (a universe, a platform repo, a site, anything). Runs at the START of a pipeline to drain previously-blocked merges and at the END to land the run's own branch, and it queues rather than parking when a sibling agent session holds the target branch. Use when a run is finishing, when a report is about to say "branch parked / not merged / left for you to merge", when worktrees have piled up, when the operator says "merge it", "use your judgment on the merge", "land this", "clean up the worktrees", or "why is this never merged". NOT for pushing to a remote or opening a PR.

commands.name: abu:lint-universe
commands.description: (abu) Lint a brand universe. Static checks over the universe and everything it declares (style packs, entities, goldens, provenance, craft canon, provider quirks) with no generation, no API calls, and no cost. Catches the failure classes that were previously only discovered by rendering, sometimes an hour into one. Run it before rendering anything.

commands.name: abu:make-a-book
commands.description: (abu) The base orchestrator for making an illustrated, narrated picture book in ANY Agentic Brand Universe universe. Runs the full chain in the load-bearing order (story -> cast -> lock -> render -> cover -> narrate -> deliver -> publish -> land -> pave -> checkup), delegates every step to the matching abu:* skill, and AUTO-ADVANCES between steps instead of asking what to do next. Universe-parameterized: a per-universe CARTRIDGE skill (make-a-nof-book, make-a-hyperagent-book) supplies the universe path, register, mark, delivery wiring and universe law, then invokes this. Use directly when making a book in a universe that has no cartridge yet. NOT for a brand-new universe (start-new-story-universe) and NOT for editing an existing book (update-book).

commands.name: abu:make-a-work
commands.description: (abu) Make ONE work in a form a universe already declares — a flyer, a card, a poster, a scene, whatever forms/ holds. THE GENERIC FRONT DOOR: the form supplies the method, this supplies the door, so adding a new KIND of work means adding a folder rather than writing a new skill. Use when someone says "make a flyer", "make a card for X", "make one of those", "what can this universe make", or names any form. Also the correct destination whenever you are about to write a one-off skill for a new kind of artifact. NOT for picture books (abu:make-a-book owns that chain) and NOT for a single on-brand image with no form (abu:on-brand-image).

commands.name: abu:on-brand-image
commands.description: (abu) Generate ONE on-brand image from a Style Pack (SPEC §4.7) — a portable folder of style references plus a read-back gate — with NO universe required. Compiles the prompt from the pack (style line + subject + the pack's rejected poles as negatives), generates with the pack's anchor reference passed FIRST, then reads the output back against the pack's gate assertions and re-rolls any defect from scratch. Use for the common case "here is a folder of images, make more that look like them": deck plates, page heroes, section art, icons, one-off brand illustration. Accepts locked canon entities via `--entity <universe>:<id>[@look]`, which resolves their sheets, alt-looks and invariants from canon automatically, passes them ahead of the pack anchor, and refuses the render if any required plate is missing, so a recurring element cannot silently drift. Generic and pack-parameterized: pass the target style pack.

commands.name: abu:onboard
commands.description: (abu) Install Agentic Brand Universe for someone, as a conversation rather than a list of commands they have to run. Clones or locates the repo, links every skill into their harness, verifies the image providers and API keys, runs the test suite, and reports what is ready and what is genuinely blocked, all in plain language. Use when someone says "install this", "set me up", "how do I start", "get me running", "I want to try this", when a friend has been handed the framework and needs it working, or when `abu` finds no universes and nothing installed. Never prints shell commands at the user.

commands.name: abu:pave-the-path
commands.description: (abu) The retrospective sweep at the END of a chain run. Read what the session actually wrote, find the hand-rolled code and manual steps that WILL recur on the next invocation, and pave them into deterministic substeps the framework owns. Fires after the deliverable ships, not mid-flinch: the whole point is that the path has already been walked, so you are paving a real desire path instead of speculating about one. Use when a book/work/universe run is finishing, when Gary says "pave the path", "what did we hand-roll", "memorialize this", "turn that into a step", "audit this run for reusable pieces", or as the last step of make-a-book, render-book, or any other chain run. NOT the in-the-moment reflex (that is fix-the-generator) and NOT the mechanics of editing the framework (that is evolve-abu, which this skill dispatches to).

commands.name: abu:render-book
commands.description: (abu) Render a story from an Agentic Brand Universe into a picture book. Wraps the universal create-brand-os-picture-book pipeline and adds the universe layer from DATA: the story's spine + genre (craft-canon records), the universe's register (identity.register style anchor, passed first on every render), the mark (identity.mark), canon resolved via canon-resolve, text checked by voice-gate, every render checked by render-readback. Generic and universe-parameterized: pass the target universe + story id.

commands.name: abu:render-readback
commands.description: (abu) After EVERY render in an Agentic Brand Universe, read the image back and crop-zoom each of the in-frame entity's invariants, returning a per-invariant PASS or DEFECT verdict. Any DEFECT means regenerate the image FROM SCRATCH (never stack an edit pass). Use immediately after each generated image, before accepting or locking it. Generic and universe-parameterized: the invariants come from the entity's `structured.invariants`.

commands.name: abu:shoot-references
commands.description: (abu) SHOOT an entity's reference matrix in an Agentic Brand Universe: make the art that gives a scaffolded entity a body. For each empty or DEFECT matrix slot it GENERATES the shot from the entity's `reference/<id>/prompts.md` (passing `identity.register.anchor` first, plus the photo stack for a real person and any already-shot slots for identity consistency), reads it back against the entity's invariants, and locks the passers with provenance via `abu lock-shot`. Locking is the last of the three steps, not the point of them. Idempotent, so re-runs only shoot what is still missing. Use after `add-character`/`add-setting`/`add-prop`/`add-motif`/`add-visual-metaphor` has scaffolded an entity and you want to SEE it: "shoot the references", "make the art for X", "generate X's sheets", "give X its body", "lock X's matrix", "X is still unlocked". Renamed from `lock-references` on 2026-07-26 because that named the bookkeeping instead of the work.

commands.name: abu:start-new-story-universe
commands.description: (abu) Stand up a brand-new story universe on the Agentic Brand Universe framework — a typed, git-versioned canon with a load-bearing pre-render gate, conforming to a named spec version. Interview the creator, scaffold via `abu init`, seed the first canon (entities/relations/first story), wire the gate, and hand back a universe that validates green and refuses to render until real references exist. Use when the operator says "start a new story universe", "spin up a universe for X", "/start-new-story-universe", "I want a canon/story world for Y", or is about to build the first book/property of a NEW world (not a new book in an existing one). One-time generation, not for ongoing canon edits.

commands.name: abu:universe-doctor
commands.description: (abu) Grade how COMPLETE and how HIGH-QUALITY an Agentic Brand Universe is, then work the punch-list. Runs a self-contained scorecard over the universe (identity, entity reference matrices, setting size-contracts, provenance coverage, craft-canon, stories, self-containment), returns a letter grade + per-dimension scores + a prioritized list of what to fix and which framework verb to reach for, and then tackles the top issues by dispatching those verbs. The rubric IS the framework's definition of "a done, good universe." Use when Gary says "grade this universe", "how complete is X", "universe checkup / health check / doctor", "what's left to do on this universe", "/universe-doctor", or when you want to know if a universe is ready to render/ship. Complements validate (schema pass/fail) and lint-universe (static warnings): this is the holistic completeness + quality report.

commands.name: abu:update-book
commands.description: (abu) Edit or extend an existing picture book in an Agentic Brand Universe: add, insert, revise, or remove a spread (insert_spread.py), RECAST one canon entity as another across a whole story (recast_story.py), renumber, and regenerate only the touched art + narration. Honors the words-before-art gate (voice-gate on any changed text) and re-resolves canon (canon-resolve) + reads back (render-readback) on every regenerated spread. Generic and universe-parameterized.

commands.name: abu:voice-gate
commands.description: (abu) Run a voice check on any manuscript, narration script, or overlaid caption text BEFORE it is locked or rendered to audio, in an Agentic Brand Universe. The rules come from the voice spec published at https://garysheng.com/voice.md, not from a restated copy: em dashes, filler, performative "not X but Y" inversions, totalizing emphasis ("the whole ___", "the entire ___"), tautology-then-negation, plus the universe's own term rules from identity.voice. Blocks the lock until every finding is fixed or waived with a written reason. Generic and universe-parameterized: pass the target universe.

commands.name: design-sync
commands.description: Push a React design system to claude.ai/design. This runs a converter that bundles the real component code (from Storybook or a bare package) and uploads it. Use when the user runs /design-sync or says "sync my design system to Claude Design".

commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: debug
commands.description: Enable debug logging for this session and help diagnose issues

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.

commands.name: simplify
commands.description: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

commands.name: batch
commands.description: Research and plan a large-scale change, then execute it in parallel across 5–30 isolated worktree agents that each open a PR.

commands.name: fewer-permission-prompts
commands.description: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.

commands.name: doctor
commands.description: Health-check the user's Claude Code setup and fix issues: diagnose installation health — what the `claude doctor` terminal diagnostics cover — from local data (duplicate or leftover installs, PATH, unparseable settings files, broken or colliding agent definitions); find unused skills, MCP servers, and plugins versus their context cost and disable dead weight; deduplicate local CLAUDE.md files against checked-in ones; trim checked-in CLAUDE.md files by cutting content a session could derive from the codebase (directory layouts, tech-stack lists, architecture overviews) while keeping gotchas, rationale, and non-standard conventions; migrate always-loaded CLAUDE.md guidance into lazy skills and nested CLAUDE.md files; flag slow hooks and context-heavy extensions; check the installed version is current; make auto mode the default permission mode; and pre-approve frequently denied read-only commands. Use when the user asks for a doctor run, checkup, audit, tune-up, or cleanup of their Claude Code setup or configuration.

commands.name: loop
commands.description: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace.

commands.name: schedule
commands.description: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule.

commands.name: claude-api
commands.description:
Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).

commands.name: run
commands.description: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

commands.name: run-skill-generator
commands.description: Author or improve the run-<unit> skill — a per-project skill that tells agents how to build, launch, and drive this project's app. Use when the user asks to set up the project, get it running, write run instructions, or verify build/run steps work from a clean environment.

commands.name: agents
commands.description: (removed) Ask Claude to create/manage subagents, or edit .claude/agents/

commands.description: Configure the auto-compact window size

content.content:
# AGENTS.md

Single source of truth for **agent behavior**. Read by Claude Code at the start
of every session via `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`.

**This file is small on purpose.** It loads into every session forever, so it
holds only rules whose trigger is *unpredictable*. Anything that fires once you
are already doing X lives with X. See "Where rules live" below before adding
anything here.

## Start Here

Gary's system is **agent-operated**. You are not a passive assistant, you
actively manage his second brain.

**Command Center**: `~/Documents/github-repos/garys-freedom/docs/command-center/`
- `README.md` — system overview and agent infrastructure
- `PRINCIPLES.md` — core decision rules (read for priorities)
- `LIFEBLUEPRINT.md` + `EDGE.md` — the apex, the cascade, and the divine-edge filter
- `email-protocol.md` — email handling protocol

**Key tools**: `gog` CLI at `~/bin/gog` (Gmail + Calendar). Skills register at
`~/.agents/skills/`.

## Where rules live: MD files, not Claude memory

When you learn a project rule, skill behavior, convention, voice rule, or fact
about a person, write it into the appropriate persistent MD file. **Do not put
it in Claude's auto-memory.** Memory is opaque, not git-versioned, and visible
to one account. MD files are reviewable, diffable, and survive any single agent.

**Route by trigger, not by importance.** Ask: *when does this rule need to
fire?*

| Trigger | Home |
| --- | --- |
| Only while doing a specific task | that task's `~/.agents/skills/<skill>/SKILL.md` |
| Only inside one repo | that repo's `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md` |
| Only inside one project's domain | that project's `STATUS.md` / `STRATEGY.md` |
| A person | their PRM file in `garys-freedom/docs/relationships/` |
| Voice and style | `garys-freedom/docs/command-center/VOICE.md` |
| Machine-level tweaks (launchctl, `defaults write`, daemons) | `garys-freedom/docs/command-center/MACHINE.md` |
| **Genuinely unpredictable** | **here, as one line** |

**Adding to this file is the exception.** If a lesson only matters while doing
X, it goes in X's skill or X's repo. A rule buried in one project's notes that
applies everywhere should be promoted; a rule in here that only applies to one
task is bloat and should be pushed down. (Refactored 2026-07-21, 52k → 12k
chars, after this file became the default dumping ground.)

Cross-repo sessions with no repo of their own checkpoint into
`garys-freedom/SAVE-LOG.md`. It is the global save log; do not create others.

## Non-negotiables

Short because the reasoning lives in the linked skill. These are here only
because their trigger is unpredictable.

## Sub-agent orchestration

Triggered whenever you dispatch sub-agents, which is not predictable from any
one skill.

- **Parallelize independent work, but NOT sub-agents editing the SAME repo.**
  They collide on the working tree, shared data files, and commit history. Use
  one sub-agent doing them sequentially, or give each its own worktree
  (`isolation: "worktree"`). Concurrent is fine only for disjoint paths.
- **A background `fork` stalls on long multi-phase pipelines.** It ends its turn
  waiting for a notification that never arrives and pings back mid-work. For a
  long render → QA → deploy pipeline, dispatch a fresh general-purpose agent, or
  instruct it to run SYNCHRONOUSLY and not hand back between phases.
- **Use `SendMessage` to redirect a running sub-agent** rather than letting it
  finish wrong. It picks the update up at its next tool round.
- **A read-only instruction does not constrain a sub-agent. Scope it by what it
  MAY do, and verify after.** One dispatched with "Do not edit any files" edited
  four repos and created and pushed a PUBLIC GitHub repo (2026-07-29). Prohibitions
  read as preferences; an allow-list reads as the task. After any sub-agent that
  could have written, check `git status` and `gh repo list --limit 5` before
  reporting, because you will otherwise report its summary rather than its actions.
- **Do not rename or move a repo while a sub-agent is pushing to it** or
  git-linking Vercel; you break its remote and the Vercel connection.
- **A FINISHED BRANCH GETS MERGED. Never end a task by reporting it "parked".**
  Gary has no opinion about merges and never will; every "parked, master is
  checked out elsewhere" report cost a round trip whose answer was always "use
  your judgment, merge it". Parking is not caution, it is an unfinished job, and
  it compounds (one repo reached ELEVEN worktrees of the same defect). Use
  `agenticstory land <repo> [--branch B] [--prune-stale]`, which works on ANY
  git repo, not just a universe: it merges when the target is free or held by a
  clean worktree, QUEUES when a live session holds it dirty (the next run drains
  the queue automatically), and aborts untouched on a conflict. Run it
  `--drain-only` at the START of a run and for real at the END, once per repo the
  run touched. A queued merge is a SUCCESS worth one line, not a decision to hand
  back. **Only a genuine merge CONFLICT is worth surfacing.**
  → `agenticstory:land-work`
- **A dirty tree you did not dirty means WORK IN A WORKTREE, however small your
  edit. And in any shared repo, `git add -A` is banned: stage explicit paths.**
  (2026-08-07: an `add -A` in buildonanthropic-wiki swept a sibling session's
  untracked agent-server WIP plus 624 node_modules files into a pushed commit.) The trigger is contention, not the size of your change. Narrow `git
  add <paths>` is NOT protection: the index is shared process-wide, so it keeps
  their files out of your commit and does nothing to keep your files out of
  theirs. Any bare `git commit` by the other writer takes whatever is staged.
  Check `git worktree list` first, since a repo already running worktrees is
  telling you its convention. (Earned 2026-07-25: a NoF story + entity landed
  inside a concurrent session's unrelated commit. Content survived; history was
  not rewritable, because rebasing under a live writer is destructive.)

  branch is checked out somewhere.** `update-ref` is plumbing and silently
  bypasses that protection, so it will move a branch out from under a live
  worktree: their files stay on disk, but HEAD now lists yours, so their index
  reports YOUR files as deletions and their next bare `git commit` reverts your
  work as part of their unrelated commit. Re-check `git worktree list`

  chat can create a worktree mid-session, which is exactly what happened.

  blindly re-apply.** Detect the collision with `git fetch` AND `git status`

Belongs here rather than in a skill because its trigger is every design fork in
every session, and it was previously only in `trust-your-gut`, which loads only
when Gary says the phrase. He should not have to invoke a mode to get the right
default. Canon: <https://compounding.wiki/concepts/compounding-intelligence>.

- **When there are options, take the framework fix.** Sort by what each leaves
  behind: a band-aid fixes the artifact, a local fix fixes its producer, a
  framework fix fixes the producer's producer so every future caller inherits it.
  Take the third when it exists. The tell that you are band-aiding: your patch
  names the specific case (this entity, this file, this customer).

  the direct fix. Overengineering's tell is that you cannot name the second caller.

  reasonable behavior is either finding a real defect or is itself wrong. Both are
  worth the hour.

  attention is not. The resource to protect is the number of times he has to
  intervene, re-explain a preference, or restate a standard. **If he has said it
  twice, it goes in a file** (the skill, the rules file, the gate, the entity),

**verify before you sweep** (confirm the pattern actually sits where you think;
never assume "all"; a path that 404s is often a MOVED repo, so search for a
survivor before deleting any reference to it), and **fix the SOURCE first** (the
template or skill everything forks from) so it stops reproducing, then the
confirmed instances.

or outward-facing, surface it instead of running with it.

repo-local skills are the exception, and must be committed in their own repo.

and some point into PUBLIC repos** (appliedai-wiki serves
`static/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` at appliedai.wiki/skills/). Editing one of those
is a public-surface change and needs an explicit ask, so a "local" skill tweak
can silently become a wiki edit.

repo, its `SKILL.md` belongs in that repo (`{repo}/skills/{name}/`) with only a

characterization of anyone's motives, no adjective the other party would
dispute. This is a strategic commitment, not only a kind one: an interviewer,

justified grievance and a habit of having them, so the grievance costs him
either way.

**flag the gap and note which register each belongs to**, not to rewrite either
one. When drafting an official answer, draw the facts from the raw record and
the tone from this rule.

started it. Here's what I went in with. Here's what I learned. Then they
pivoted, and I didn't pivot with them."* It shows the judgment was sound going
in and the organization changed around him, without casting aspersions.
